metadata.name: wget
metadata.description: Download files from HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP servers

installation.note: wget is installed by default on most Linux distributions

overview.summary: wget (web get) downloads files from the internet using HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP protocols. It's a non-interactive downloader - perfect for scripts and automated downloads. wget can resume interrupted downloads, download entire websites, and handle authentication.

syntax.description: Download file from URL. wget saves file with original name or specified name.

options.description: Write output to file with specified name
options.use_case: Save file with custom name instead of original
Resume interrupted download (very useful for large files)

breakdown.behavior: Checks if file exists, resumes from end if partial
breakdown.useful: Essential for large files that may get interrupted
breakdown.time_saver: Saves time - doesn't restart from beginning

output_explanation.notes: Resumes interrupted download. Very useful for large files. wget checks existing file and continues from where it stopped.

examples.use_case: Resume large file downloads that were interrupted

output_explanation.notes: Downloads file to specified directory. Creates directory if it doesn't exist. Useful for organizing downloads.

misconceptions.title: wget requires interactive input
misconceptions.reality: wget is non-interactive - it runs automatically without prompts. Perfect for scripts and automated downloads.
misconceptions.tip: wget is non-interactive - great for scripts. Use curl if you need more interactive features.

common_pitfalls.description: Restarting download from beginning if interrupted
common_pitfalls.solution: Always use wget -c for large files. It resumes from where it stopped, saving time and bandwidth.

common_pitfalls.description: File saved in current directory instead of intended location
common_pitfalls.solution: Use -P directory/ to specify download location, or cd to desired directory first.

related_commands.relationship: Download tool; wget for simple downloads, curl for advanced HTTP
related_commands.description: Transfer data with URLs (more features than wget)

related_commands.relationship: Package download; apt downloads packages, wget downloads files
related_commands.description: Download and install packages (apt uses wget/curl internally)

best_practices: Use wget -c for large files (resume capability)
Use -P to download to specific directory
Use -q for quiet mode in scripts
Verify downloads with checksums when available
performance_tips: Use -c to resume instead of restarting large downloads
wget handles redirects and authentication automatically

additional_notes.non_interactive: wget is non-interactive - perfect for scripts and automated downloads
additional_notes.resume: Use -c flag to resume interrupted downloads - very useful for large files
additional_notes.common_patterns: Common: wget URL (simple), wget -O name URL (rename), wget -c URL (resume), wget -P dir/ URL (directory)
additional_notes.vs_curl: wget = simple downloads, curl = advanced HTTP client. wget is better for simple file downloads.
